The title designates the poem as the account (*apadāna*) of a senior monk (*thera*) who made a past offering of an upper robe or garment (*uttareyya*). The text also shares substantial stock verse material with other poems within the Therāpadāna itself, including the *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 24 and Tha-Ap 562), *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425 and Tha-Ap 254), *Ukkhittapadumiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 342), and *Ekadussadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 336) [DharmaNexus].
